title: Casper and the Vow
premise: Noor Reyes keeps her late grandfather's lighthouse on the coast of Marrow Bay, writing romance novels under a pen name and answering a decade of letters from a stranger known only as 'C.' When C — Elias Casper Vane, a cartographer with a degenerative memory condition — moves into the cottage next door, Noor realizes the man who taught her to be brave through paper is losing the ability to hold onto her in person. As they fall in love against the ticking clock of his diagnosis, Noor must choose between guarding her rebuilt heart and lending it entirely. In the end, she stops waiting for him to remember their story and instead builds one he can live inside: they marry at the lighthouse, and though his memories fray, the vow — recorded, rewritten, renewed each morning — becomes the thing that outlasts forgetting.
about_author: Felix Voss is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing lighthouse logs before turning to fiction. They write love stories about people who keep things — lights, letters, promises — and believe the bravest endings are the quiet ones.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Seven years after a fire took her grandfather and nearly took her, Noor tends the Marrow Bay light, writes novels under a pen name, and rereads a decade of letters from 'C,' the anonymous correspondent who once talked her out of despair. Beat: safety as a cage she's made comfortable.

chapters.title: A Moving Truck in November
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A new tenant takes the neighboring cottage: Elias Casper Vane, a cartographer with careful manners and a notebook he never lets leave his pocket. He doesn't recognize her name; she doesn't yet recognize his middle name. Beat: the first tremor of fate disguised as coincidence.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Casper unpacks boxes of maps and one shoebox of unsent drafts — his own letters, copies of every one he mailed to a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter. His neurologist has given him a timeline. Beat: he came to find her before he forgets why.

chapters.title: Tea, Tide Tables, and Almost
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Neighboring routines collide — shared tea, borrowed tide tables, an argument about whether the old light should be automated. Casper quotes a line from her letters back to her without realizing its source. Beat: recognition dawning like a tide she can't stop.

chapters.title: C Is for Casper
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She finds his draft letters while returning a borrowed book and confronts him on the cliff path. The truth comes out: ten years of correspondence, and he never told her because the first letter was meant to be an apology for something he no longer remembers doing. Beat: wonder curdling into hurt.

chapters.title: The Apology He Can't Recall
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Casper searches his early notebooks for what he apologized for and finds only gaps — pages from the year of the fire. He confesses his diagnosis instead: a degenerative condition erasing recent memory first, old wounds last. Beat: honesty as the only gift he has left to give.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Terrified but unable to walk away, Noor proposes terms: friendship, nothing more, because she has survived one great loss already. They begin a ritual of morning walks where she tells him yesterday, every day, in case tomorrow he can't. Beat: love rationed into safe portions.

chapters.title: The Map of Us
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Casper begins mapping their days — hand-drawn charts of the bay annotated with moments: where Noor laughed, where she cried, where she kissed his knuckles. He hides the atlas in the lighthouse. Beat: a man building an anchor against the flood.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A winter gale knocks out the automated backup, and Noor must run the light manually through the night. Casper stays, holding lanterns and her hands, and in the calm eye of the storm they cross the line they drew. Beat: passion arriving like weather — undeniable, uninvited.

chapters.title: Morning, Again
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Casper wakes and doesn't know the woman asleep beside him — the first lost day. Panic, then the atlas, then Noor reading their story aloud until his shoulders unknot. Beat: grief and tenderness sharing one bed.

chapters.title: Her Sister's Verdict
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor's pragmatic sister Imogen arrives for the holidays and sees the situation plainly: Noor is falling for a man with an expiration date. A fierce argument in the kitchen ends with Imogen's warning — you're repeating the fire, choosing to lose someone again. Beat: doubt voiced by the person who loves her most.

chapters.title: The Year of the Fire
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Casper finally decodes his oldest apology: he was the off-duty coast guard trainee whose misfiled report delayed responders the night of the fire. He was there. He wrote the first letter as penance. Beat: the past arrives, and it is worse than either imagined.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Penance
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor learns the truth and shatters — the stranger who saved her with letters is the stranger whose error cost her grandfather. She banishes him from the lighthouse and burns nothing but her own manuscript pages. Beat: the wound beneath the wound.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Casper prepares to leave Marrow Bay, giving the atlas to Imogen for safekeeping, but a memory lapse strands him on the cliff road at night. He walks toward the only light he trusts. Beat: the letter-writer becomes the man lost at sea.

chapters.title: Rescue
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor finds him half-frozen below the light, reciting her first letter from memory — the one thing the disease hasn't touched. She carries him home and sits vigil, furious and undone. Beat: hatred failing against love in the body before the mind agrees.

chapters.title: Forgiveness Is a Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At his hospital bedside, Noor reads his decade of letters end to end and understands: he didn't cause the fire; he carried it. Forgiveness isn't absolution, she realizes — it's choosing to keep the light on anyway. Beat: the whole heart, finally lent.

chapters.title: What Time Is Already Taking
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Casper's decline accelerates; he loses whole weeks and begins confusing Noor with her letters, calling her 'the girl in the envelope.' He asks her to leave him before he becomes a stranger who hurts her. Beat: the antagonist is time itself, and it is winning.

chapters.title: The Vow, Draft One
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Refusing to be protected from love, Noor proposes marriage — not despite his memory, but built around it: vows written to be read fresh each morning, a life designed to be fallen into daily. He says yes through tears. Beat: defiance dressed as devotion.

chapters.title: Imogen Objects
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Imogen threatens to contest the marriage, convinced Noor is sacrificing herself to a fantasy. Their confrontation cracks open Imogen's own buried grief, and she relents — not with approval, but with a promise to be there. Beat: family mended at the cost of honesty.

chapters.title: The Light Between Two Days
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. On the eve of the wedding, Casper suffers his worst episode yet and wakes believing Noor is a nurse and the wedding a kindness she invented. He tries to release her from the promise. Beat: the darkest hour, when even hope seems like a symptom.

chapters.title: Say It Again, Say It Always
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the lighthouse, before the town and the turning beam, Noor answers his doubt the only way that works: she says the vow, and he repeats it, and they keep saying it until he believes it — then the gathered guests say it with them, so the words exist outside his head forever. Beat: climax — memory outsourced to love itself.

chapters.title: Every Morning, the Same Sea
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, one year later. Mornings at the cottage: coffee, the atlas, the vow read aloud, Casper sometimes knowing her, always choosing her anew. Noor's new novel — their story — is finished, dedicated 'to C, who kept writing.' Beat: resolution — belonging not remembered but remade, daily, against the tide.
